r.정치 구도: The president is directly elected, while the day-to-day running of the country falls to a prime minister and cabinet chosen by parliament. The president can veto bills, and overriding a veto takes a three-fifths majority in the lower house, so lawmaking often stalls when the president and the government come from rival camps. A pro-European centrist coalition took power after the 2023 election, but the 2025 presidential race was won by a candidate backed by the conservative Law and Justice party, setting the president against the government. Undoing court changes made under the previous conservative government, legal recognition for same-sex couples and relations with the EU are the big fault lines, and the rivalry runs on toward the 2027 parliamentary election.

t.why: Bordering Ukraine, Belarus and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad, it is the anchor of NATO's eastern defenses. Having been carved up by its powerful neighbors and erased from the map in the late 18th century, it is especially wary of Russia. It joined NATO in 1999 and the EU in 2004, and since the war in Ukraine began it has become the main route for Western weapons and aid flowing into Ukraine. Its defense spending as a share of GDP is among the highest in NATO, and it is buying tanks, howitzers and fighter jets in bulk from the United States and South Korea. Having also taken in many Ukrainian refugees, it is the big country that speaks for Eastern Europe inside the EU.
t.rel: Bordering Ukraine, Belarus and Russia's Kaliningrad exclave, it is NATO's eastern front line. Since the war in Ukraine it has raised defense spending to over 4% of GDP.
t.korea: Diplomatic relations were established in November 1989, making Poland the second former Eastern Bloc country after Hungary to recognize South Korea. After the war in Ukraine broke out in 2022, it signed huge deals for K2 tanks, K9 self-propelled howitzers, FA-50 light attack aircraft and Chunmoo multiple rocket launchers, becoming the largest customer for Korean arms exports. In 2025 it signed a second contract for 180 more K2 tanks, some of them to be built in Poland. LG Energy Solution runs Europe's largest battery plant near Wroclaw, and many Korean makers of battery materials and parts have followed it there.
t.know: Inside the Wieliczka salt mine is a chapel whose walls and chandeliers are carved from salt.
etext: Wages lower than in Western Europe and proximity to Germany have drawn plants making car parts, home appliances, furniture and batteries. Deeply woven into German supply chains, it rises and falls with the German economy.

Since switching to a market economy in the early 1990s it has grown almost without a break, apart from the 2020 pandemic. It was the only EU member to avoid a contraction in the 2009 financial crisis. It is the largest recipient of EU funds, which it has used to greatly expand its roads and railways.
Having long relied on coal for a large share of its electricity, it faces heavy carbon costs. That is why it is pursuing its first nuclear power plant and offshore wind farms in the Baltic Sea.
A shrinking population and young people leaving to work in Western Europe have caused labor shortages. Soaring defense spending is also pushing up the budget deficit and public debt.
